rule: GOAL: Rotate the plug and move it so its prongs align with the socket’s contact points. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug one grid unit; Space rotates it 90 degrees clockwise. RULE: The plug must face right and align perfectly with the socket’s two distinct contact slots. TRAP: Assuming arrow presses move multiple cells; they only move one unit, requiring careful counting to stay within the action limit.

GOAL: Catch the falling block with the paddle to guide it into the target cup. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the paddle horizontally; spacebar drops or releases the block. RULE: The block slides along the paddle surface to the nearest edge before dropping vertically. TRAP: Assuming the block falls straight down from the contact point leads to missing the cup walls.

GOAL: Place both boxes onto their respective frames. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active box; clicking a box activates it. RULE: Only the active box responds to arrow keys, requiring you to switch control between the two boxes. TRAP: Assuming one box on a frame solves the puzzle; both frames must be filled simultaneously.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over each other into empty spaces. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click the highlighted landing spot to move. RULE: A jump is only allowed if an adjacent peg blocks the path to an empty hole. TRAP: Clicking a peg that is already selected does nothing, so do not waste clicks trying to re-select it.

ESTABLISHED: The head is a four-column block; the nose is the front column. Absorbed boxes attach directly ahead. FAILED: Moving directly into a box rotates the head but does not move or absorb it. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the box location or rotating the head to face it. CONTROLS: Arrows move or rotate if blocked. Space absorbs the box ahead or drops the carried box.

GOAL: Push two boxes into their frames. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide boxes; mouse clicks select them. RULE: Sliding boxes stop only when blocked by walls or frames, not just by leaving purple zones. TRAP: Assuming a box stops immediately after exiting a purple door wastes time; it may slide further.

GOAL: Move three boxes onto the marked frame spots. CONTROLS: Arrows move and turn the head; Space absorbs or drops a box directly ahead. RULE: You can only carry one box at a time; dropping it clears your hands. TRAP: Believing you can push a box from behind wastes turns; you must absorb it first.

GOAL: Color three bars blue and position them to catch falling goo, then pour from the paddle. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the paddle; Space poured the liquid; Mouse clicks colored specific bars blue. RULE: The liquid splits upon hitting the paddle, sending droplets upward to fill the aligned blue bars above. TRAP: Thinking you must move the paddle under the source; instead, spread the goo wide so it splits and rises into the pre-positioned bars.

ESTABLISHED: Blue and yellow pieces are mated. Blue is active. Yellow body spans rows 20-41, cols 23-41. Blue body occupies rows 38-46, cols 26-34. FAILED: Rotating blue without checking overlaps. Assuming pieces pass through each other. GOAL IS NOT: Simply rotating blue in place. CONTROLS: Click selects piece. Space rotates active piece. No collision detection prevents overlap during rotation.

GOAL: Slide the plus shape into the target frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green cursor; pushing against the plus moves it. RULE: The plus slides until its arms hit a frame boundary. TRAP: Assuming the plus moves freely; it gets stuck by overlapping frame edges, requiring precise positioning to clear the block.

GOAL: Place three colored shapes into matching gray slots to clear the board. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space rotates it; Clicks select a shape. RULE: Shapes must fit perfectly into slots without overlapping other shapes or walls. TRAP: Believing rotation is free; attempting to rotate a shape into an occupied space wastes turns if the move is blocked.

GOAL: Move the goal peg to the final position. CONTROLS: Click to move the peg. RULE: You win when the peg reaches the target. TRAP: Believing the action bar is a hard limit stopped you from trying extra moves.

GOAL: Arrange three pieces to form a specific sum. CONTROLS: Arrows move, space rotates, click selects. RULE: Total value must match the target; hidden cells count. TRAP: Assuming clicks are free; each selection consumes an action.

GOAL: Stack four blue bars without touching the walls or each other to trigger the win. CONTROLS: Click a bar to grab it; use arrow keys to slide it horizontally; press space to pour. RULE: Wet goo only rises if it hits a wall or another object, so keep gaps open. TRAP: Assuming edge goo always rises; it vanishes if the gap is too narrow to form a stream.

GOAL: Slide the plus-shaped box upward into the frame opening. CONTROLS: Arrows move the character; clicks select or confirm actions. RULE: Pushing the bottom arm lifts the entire shape, aligning it with the upper slot. TRAP: Thinking the box was stuck due to side walls, when it only needed vertical clearance from below.

GOAL: Clear the puzzle by moving objects into place within thirty actions. CONTROLS: Arrows moved objects, Space rotated them, and Clicks selected them. RULE: You must select an object before moving it, and selection changes on every action. TRAP: Thinking you could move one object continuously; re-selecting it after moving others cost extra clicks.

GOAL: Move the green block into the target frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; entering the goo bounces it backward. RULE: The goo repels the block until it turns red, then becomes passable. TRAP: Thinking the goo was a solid wall; it actually requires repeated entry to trigger the color change before passing through.

ESTABLISHED: The frame border is passable. The orange oscillates unpredictably. FAILED: Pre-planning a fixed route or relying on the border to block movement. GOAL IS NOT: A static path; it requires dynamic, reactive steering of the orange. CONTROLS: Move the head to block paths, forcing the orange to turn; use SPACE to wait.

ESTABLISHED: Level 2 cleared with one remaining peg; goal adjacency enables jumps. FAILED: Assumed win condition was "empty specific region" or "all pegs in one region"; these theories contradict Level 2 timing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing a single designated area or gathering all pegs into one isolated cluster. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift goal positions on rails; clicking adjacent pegs triggers jumps over neighbors into empty cells or goals.

ESTABLISHED: Streams at 56-58 and 59-61 leak correctly. Cups 2, 3, and 4 fill as expected. No leak occurs at column 47. FAILED: Simulations incorrectly generated a leak at 47 due to an off-by-two error in right-child column calculation. GOAL IS NOT: The leak at 47 is not a required outcome; it was a simulation artifact. CONTROLS: Right-child streams originate from layer end minus two, not the layer end itself.

ESTABLISHED: Three pieces connect in a chain, yet the level does not clear. FAILED: Assuming any full chain equals a win; the game rejected this configuration. GOAL IS NOT: Simply connecting all pieces once. CONTROLS: Movement shifts pieces; rotation aligns edges. The hidden rule requires a "locked" state where no further connections are possible, meaning you must create extra overlaps, not just a simple line.

ESTABLISHED: Pushing the goo left clears the central path; vertical shafts connect upper and lower rooms; the plus block is in the top-left quadrant. FAILED: Moving right immediately hits a gray block; pushing the goo right from the start fails; crossing directly through the middle is blocked. GOAL IS NOT: The plus block itself; the goo's initial position; the gray obstacle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; pushing blocks slides them until hitting a wall or another block; phases change room layout.

GOAL: Clear the board by reducing the remaining pegs to a single survivor. CONTROLS: Click a peg to jump over an adjacent peg into an empty hole, removing the jumped piece. Use directional keys to slide goals when needed. RULE: A valid jump requires an immediate neighbor and an empty landing spot directly opposite it. TRAP: Assuming hidden off-screen pegs do not exist; they remain in the total count until captured.

GOAL: Slide objects to fill target spots without overlapping. CONTROLS: Click to select, arrows to move, space to confirm. RULE: Objects cannot pass through each other, so move vertically before horizontally to avoid blocks. TRAP: Thinking you can slide past an object; collisions stop movement instantly, forcing careful path planning.

ESTABLISHED: Two spouts feed three top cups; the left cup is a blocker, not a target. Four sheets result from two pours. FAILED: Using the left cup or purple piece to truncate flow diagonally; the diagonal rule blocks this interaction. GOAL IS NOT: Filling the left-facing cup or using it as a simple wall. CONTROLS: Bars and the purple L shift horizontally; pours activate spouts. One pour remains.

ESTABLISHED: The ferry goal carries exactly one peg at a time. FAILED: Merging pegs in the right region before boarding, as it leaves no pieces to jump over. GOAL IS NOT: A container for multiple pegs or a static blocker. CONTROLS: Left and Down move the goals along their rails; jumping over a piece captures it and lands on the next empty cell.

GOAL: Navigate the green block to the target frame in the bottom room. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step per press. RULE: The block slides through open space until hitting a wall or goo. TRAP: Pressing UP before being directly over the goo fails to trigger the necessary vertical slide.

ESTABLISHED: The level auto-resets to its initial state upon failure, but completed levels remain saved. The action bar depletes with every step, including blocked moves. FAILED: Attempting to cross specific hazard zones or finding a valid path through the current layout without exhausting the step limit. GOAL IS NOT: To preserve the current mid-level state through a reset, as the level resets completely. CONTROLS: Directional keys move the character or fail silently if blocked. The step counter decreases with every input, triggering a reset when empty.

GOAL: Park the rider precisely on the yellow frame at the corridor's end. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the rider; spacebar executes jumps over adjacent markers. RULE: A valid jump requires an immediate marker followed by an empty landing space. TRAP: Assuming the rider could land on the frame directly; it must first clear the barrier to reach the target zone.

ESTABLISHED: Riding captures pegs; markers allow hopping. Goals move along rails; off-screen goals may block movement. FAILED: Precise pathing exceeded step limits, causing resets. GOAL IS NOT: Simple single-click interactions; static positioning. CONTROLS: Click rider then target to capture. Arrow keys move all goals simultaneously.

GOAL: Slide the piston down to mate its cap with the E piece. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles the piston’s height. RULE: The piston’s cap only fits when fully extended to maximum length. TRAP: Assuming the piston stays rigid; it actually expands vertically before mating.

GOAL: Clear the level by moving the player to the exit using only four directional actions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in the corresponding direction. RULE: Each move consumes one action; you must reach the goal within the limit. TRAP: Thinking you can undo moves or that extra steps are allowed wastes actions.

ESTABLISHED: Orange stays stuck inside the frame forever. FAILED: Moving orange, placing boxes on the left, and chasing the head with white boxes. GOAL IS NOT: Placing all five boxes or filling the frame slots. CONTROLS: SPACE activates boxes; the head moves with arrow keys.
